numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In CVXOPT inequality presolve, compress_matrix treated a row as redundant whenever it was any scalar multiple of a kept row with matching right-hand-side ratio, including negative multiples; for Gx <= h a negative multiple describes the opposite half-space, so dropping it enlarged the feasible set (e.g. min z s.t. z <= 1, z >= 1 plus duplicated equalities was reported unbounded instead of optimal at 1). Separately, when presolve merged duplicate inequality rows, duals were recovered as P_leq @ z, giving every merged row a scaled copy of the full compressed multiplier; duplicated constraints received duals summing to (1 + ratio^2) times the correct value (e.g. z >= 1 stated twice produced duals 1.0 and 1.0 where the sum must be 1.0).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Only positive-ratio rows should be merged, so the problem is reported optimal at 1. Recovered duals should satisfy stationarity G_orig.T @ y_orig == G_compr.T @ z, i.e. each compressed dual is assigned entirely to the kept row and zero to dropped duplicates, so the duals of duplicated constraints sum to the correct value (1.0 in the z >= 1 example).
trigger_conditions: CVXOPT solver used with a problem whose inequality rows contain duplicate or scaled-duplicate rows that presolve merges
